 The Spurs will be without Devin Vassell for Monday’s game, as he’s out with an adductor injury. Champagnie will fill the void in the starting lineup and is worth streaming, especially for fantasy managers needing three-pointers.

 Devin Vassell (groin) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Suns. 
 Vassell is dealing with left adductor tightness, casting some doubt on his availability for Monday. Julian Champagnie could be the replacement in the starting lineup if Vassell can’t play. 
 Julian Champagnie 
 SAS 
 Forward 
 #30 
 Julian Champagnie tallied 14 points (4-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, and four three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Trail Blazers. 
 Champagnie made four of the Spurs’ 17 three-pointers on Saturday, the second time this season he’s made at least that many in a game. While the rebounds were solid, Champagnie is most valuable to managers needing points and three-pointers. Tobias Harris’ continued absence makes Champagnie a little more important for offensive spacing reasons, but he’s only worth a look in deep leagues. 
 Devin Vassell 
 SAS 
 Guard-Forward 
 #24 
 Devin Vassell notched 15 points (4-of-8 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Trail Blazers. 
 One of three Spurs starters to make multiple three-pointers, Vassell is averaging 1.6 per game this season. Despite his low field-goal percentage, the Spurs wing provides solid middle-round value in 12-team formats. With the Spurs playing four games next week, Vassell may be worth a look for those needing three-pointers and steals, as he’s available in 48 percent of Yahoo leagues. 
 Devin Vassell 
 SAS 
 Guard-Forward 
 #24 
 Devin Vassell with 21 points (8-of-18 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, three steals and a three against the Jazz. 
 Vassell made some big shots in the fourth quarter to keep the Spurs in this game. While it was a good performance, he’s only up to 12.6 points, 4 rebounds, and 3.8 assists on the season. He’s a points and 3-point streamer who will occasionally have good games but is not a must in most redraft leagues. There’s too many high usage players on the team for him to be able to score like this consistently. 
 Devin Vassell 
 SAS 
 Guard-Forward 
 #24 
 Devin Vassell amassed 14 points (5-of-11 FGs), four rebounds, eight assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Kings. 
 Four of the five Spurs starters recorded at least five assists, with Vassell leading with eight. That tally was one less than his total in San Antonio’s first three games, and in 2025-26 Vassell recorded five assists or more in six games. Simply put, fantasy managers should treat his assist output as a bonus, not an occurrence that could become the norm. 
 Julian Champagnie 
 SAS 
 Forward 
 #30 
 Julian Champagnie tallied 26 points (9-of-14 FGs), three rebounds, three assists and eight three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Kings. 
 Champagnie put on a shooting clinic during the first half, making eight of his ten three-point attempts. That tied the Spurs franchise record for most three-pointers in a half, which was previously held by...Champagnie. Also, his six three-pointers in the second quarter tied the franchise record for most in a quarter, joining Manu Ginobili, Bryn Forbes and Harrison Barnes. The move to the bench has lowered Champagnie’s fantasy ceiling, but he remains a solid option for managers needing three-pointers. 
 Tobias Harris 
 SAS 
 Forward 
 #23 
 Tobias Harris (calf) has been ruled out against the Kings on Tuesday. 
 Harris will miss another game with this calf injury, making this three straight to open the season. Dylan Harper and Devin Vassell will both continue to start, delaying head coach Mitch Johnson from having to make a tough decision on his lineup for at least one more game.

 Aday Mara notched 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, two assists and one block in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 For the first time in his young NBA career, Mara played over 30 minutes in a game. He logged 32 minutes against the Trail Blazers, but the final stat line wasn’t strong enough to make the rookie a must-start in all leagues. Mara replaced Kenrich Williams (11/2/2 with one block and two three-pointers) in the starting lineup, and who starts moving forward may be dictated by the opposition’s rotation.

 Alex Caruso accounted for 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 The Thunder didn’t have Ajay Mitchell for Wednesday’s game, opening a spot in the starting lineup for Caruso. He took advantage of the opportunity, shooting 4-of-5 from beyond the arc. Caruso’s 14 points were a new season high for him, as he totaled 17 points in the first four games he played upon returning from an ankle injury. If Mitchell remains out for Friday’s game against the Clippers, Caruso would be worth rostering in 14-team leagues and some 12-team leagues.

 Isaiah Hartenstein accumulated 20 points (10-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, six assists and two steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 After totaling 19 points in Oklahoma City’s first five games of November, Hartenstein recorded his first 20-point game of the season on Wednesday. The negative for iHart was the turnovers, of which he was responsible for six. A few of the turnovers were due to offensive fouls, so there isn’t much to worry about there. Rostered in 83 percent of Yahoo leagues, Hartenstein is providing top-100 fantasy value, slightly better than his ADP.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander produced 31 points (9-of-20 FGs, 13-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
 Gilgeous-Alexander has scored at least 30 points in six games this season. Unfortunately for him and the Thunder, the team’s lack of established scorers proved costly in both losses to the Trail Blazers. Five other Thunder players scored in double figures, with Isaiah Hartenstein’s 20 leading the way. The lack of creators who can take some of the pressure off of Gilgeous-Alexander was evident in both losses to the Trail Blazers. He’ll remain an elite fantasy option, but SGA’s ceiling may have taken a slight hit because a few of his teammates are injured.

 While Lillard didn’t lead the way offensively for the Trail Blazers as he did in Wednesday’s win over Oklahoma City, the production remained solid. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of Portland’s first 11 games, and Dame has started every game. As long as he stays healthy, Lillard should be able to deliver a top-100 season, if not more.

 Deni Avdija tallied 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, four steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
 One night removed from scoring 24 points in a win over the Thunder, Avdija was just as productive in the rematch. The 28 points were the most he’s scored in a game since November 2, when the Trail Blazers forward hit that number in a win over the Nuggets. While there were questions before the season began about Portland’s offensive pecking order, there haven’t been any issues so far, even when the currently injured Ja Morant was healthy. That’s great for those who used a top-50 draft pick on Avdija. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 De’Anthony Melton finished Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers.
 Melton’s final stat line wasn’t much to write home about, but his role may expand for Friday’s game against the Spurs. Stephen Curry left Wednesday’s game with an abdominal injury and is expected to undergo an MRI on Thursday. If Curry misses time, Melton will have a larger role, whether he moves into the starting lineup or continues to come off the bench.
